Stand up, roll your shoulders back, and let your arms hang loose for ten seconds.
Walk to the furthest room in your home or office and back.
Look out a window at something at least 20 feet away for 20 seconds — your eyes have been focused close-up for a while.
Stretch your arms overhead, interlace your fingers, and lean gently side to side.
Stand up and touch your toes, or get as close as feels good.
Drop your chin to your chest, then slowly roll your head in a half-circle to loosen your neck.
Plant your feet, place your hands on your lower back, and lean backward into a gentle stretch.
Stand up and walk up and down a flight of stairs if you have one nearby.
Shake out your wrists and hands — they've been doing all the typing.
Stand, reach one arm across your chest, and hold it with the other for ten seconds. Switch sides.
Get a glass of water and drink it standing up, away from the screen.
Step outside, even just to a doorway, and take five slow breaths.
Stand up and do ten slow bodyweight squats.
Clasp your hands behind your back and gently pull your shoulder blades together.
Close your eyes for thirty seconds and just listen to the room.
